text: {"observations": "Image 1 shows broadband noise that swells and recedes in a regular cycle over the 23.1 s clip. There are loud broadband surges at roughly 0-2 s, 7-10 s and 14-17 s, with energy reaching up to about 8 kHz. Between them come quieter troughs at roughly 3-6 s, 11-13 s and 18-21 s, where energy stays mostly below about 2.4 kHz, with a faint band near 1.5 kHz. This periodic wash pattern, about 7 s per cycle, is typical of waves breaking and receding on a shore. There are no horn, engine or voice harmonics, which argues against a city street (A) or a marketplace (B). Wind (D) would tend to be more irregular and concentrated at low frequencies, rather than showing regular full-band surges. The evidence points to a calm beach.", "answer": "C"}
